sections.overview: The Lesser Black-backed Gull breeds widely in Eurasia and winters along coasts and inland waters. It shares genus Larus with the Common Gull and Glaucous Gull profiled here.
sections.identification: Adults are long-winged gulls with dark grey backs and yellow legs. Against pale Larus hyperboreus, the dark back and yellow legs are useful contrasts.
sections.habitat: It breeds on coastal cliffs, dunes, marshy heaths and buildings, then winters on coasts, estuaries, lakes and reservoirs.
sections.diet: This omnivore eats fish, molluscs, worms and insects, as well as carrion and discarded food.
sections.behavior: It is a partial migrant, often traveling overland, and commonly follows fishing boats or feeds at ports and rubbish tips.
sections.reproduction: Pairs nest in colonies, usually on the ground; both adults build the nest and incubate the clutch.
sections.ecology: Its scavenging links marine fisheries, coastal settlements and inland feeding areas.
sections.conservation: The IUCN UK Peatland Programme lists the species as Amber in the UK, a regional designation rather than a global status.
